correctness.rationale: For each possible number a of selected hubs (0, 1, 2), permutations within the two vertex classes prove reduction to a single follower Laplacian. Its exact spectrum is determined by a 2x2 block (when both classes remain), and the inverse-square trace gives the three displayed rational costs; empty classes agree by direct calculation. The differences J1-J2, J0-J2, J0-J1 are single-crossing on q>=k: the first is quadratic with increasing numerator, the second has positive derivative, and the third has a demonstrated positive derivative bound. Ordering these crossings proves all global minimizers and ties. Scaling q/k->c gives distinct ratios alpha and 1+sqrt(2), proving an asymptotically nonempty one-hub regime. Exact-fraction grounded inversions and enumerations in verify.py corroborate but do not substitute for the proof. Possible numerical or algebra transcription errors are tested independently.

value.rationale: The complete all-budget classification in the natural two-hub biclique family reveals an intermediate mixed-class leader allocation which neither an inverse-trace classification of this family nor an inverse-square classification of almost-balanced bicliques implies. It gives exact, constant-time comparisons for every q>=k>=2 and resolves all possible tie patterns, with two distinct linear-scale thresholds. This is a structural phase portrait of a control-theoretic inverse-square variance criterion rather than a single graph example or a computation of known spectra.
